name: Protect log integrity or document the accepted position
description: Place security logs beyond the reach of administrators of the systems they record, or record a reasoned decision that the entity's threat model does not warrant it.

steps.action: Identify who can delete or alter log data, and whether that overlaps with administrators of the monitored systems.
Forward logs to a separate account, project, or tenant those administrators cannot reach.
Enforce retention through a platform lifecycle policy that cannot be shortened locally.
Where separation is impractical, record the accepted position with its rationale and an expiry for review.
Align the logging policy with whichever position was taken, so the document does not claim protection the deployment lacks.

implementation_considerations: Architectural separation via a dedicated logging account is usually cheaper and stronger than immutability features, and is available on every major platform.
Small teams often cannot separate these duties at all. A documented accepted position is a legitimate outcome and better than a policy claim the deployment does not support.
typical_duration: Days to weeks, depending on whether log routing must be rebuilt.
prerequisites: Visibility of who holds delete rights over the log store

verification_method.how: Confirm that principals administering monitored systems cannot delete or alter the corresponding logs, or that an authorised, time-bounded accepted position is on record.

residual_risk_note: Separation bounds tampering by system administrators; it does not protect against compromise of the logging platform itself.
period_limitation_note: Protecting logs now says nothing about the integrity of logs already collected during an elapsed period.
notes: Log immutability is named nowhere in the criteria. This is a DriftGuard recommendation, and a documented accepted position closes the observation.
